newsitem.title: UK: Central Asian cotton output well behind schedule.
newsitem.headline: Central Asian cotton output well behind schedule.

text.p: Cotton output in Central Asia is well behind schedule due to late harvests, disruptive weather conditions and pest infestations, according to industry journal Cotton Outlook.
At end-September Uzbekistan had harvested around two-thirds of the amount of seed cotton taken at the same time in 1995, due to late planting, the report said.
Turkmenistan has collected less than a third of the amount of cotton harvested by the same point in the 1995 season.
On 30 September 1995, deliveries of Turkmenistan cotton hit 713,180 tonnes but at the same date in 1996 only 218,489 tonnes had reached the cotton gins.
Some sources described the condition of Turkmenistan's current crop as "poor".
Tajikistan's seed cotton producing provinces had delivered between 21 and 28 percent of their output targets to state collection points.
Khotlonsk, the largest of Tajikistan's cotton regions, suffered the most signficant shortfall (21 percent) due to pest infestation, the report said.
